title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Terminology: the pushout I×Ṫ ∪_{{0}×Ṫ} Y is the mapping cylinder of f, not the mapping cone. 'C(f)' / 'cône de l'application' would normally denote the cone, where Ṫ×{1} is also collapsed. Mathematically everything on the page refers to the cylinder.
Minor gap: continuity of the induced I-action on C(f) uses that I×(quotient map) is again a quotient map. This holds because I is compact Hausdorff (Whitehead's lemma), but it is not stated.
Implicit: (c) forces Ṫ∩Y=∅ and 1·x=x (unitality of the action). Unitality is presumably part of 'opération du monoïde' but is not spelled out.
The marginal name 'cône sur Y' is somewhat misleading: T is a cylinder over Ṫ that is collapsed onto Y, i.e. a fibrewise cone over Y only when f is a bundle.

ideas.what: Abstract conical/tubular neighbourhood of Y defined as a space with a continuous action of the multiplicative monoid [0,1], fixing Y, contracting into Y, with a closed 'boundary' Ṫ such that T is the pushout I×Ṫ ∪ Y
ideas.modern_name: Mapping cylinder neighbourhood; cone/scaling structure as in conically smooth stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mapping cylinder neighbourhoods: Siebenmann (1972), Quinn (Homotopically stratified sets, 1988), Hughes and others. Scaling-action formulation: Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017) for conically smooth structures. Control data / tubes: Thom, Mather (1970).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tubular neighbourhoods and 'dévissage' of tame stratified spaces in outline, but not this axiomatic form.

ideas.what: Equivalence: monoid-action data (a), (b), (c) ⇔ the mapping-cylinder structure of f:Ṫ→Y with f(x)=0·x; boundary and interior recovered from the action (T° = ⋃_{λ<1} λT)
ideas.modern_name: Mapping cylinder as I-monoid space / pushout characterisation

ideas.what: Marginal remark that the pushout axiom (c) makes the axiom 0·T⊂Y redundant

missed.claim: Encoding a stratum's tubular neighbourhood as a continuous action of the multiplicative monoid [0,1] is essentially the device later used to define conical charts and 'unzipping'. The cylinder/cone carries a scaling action, as in Ayala–Francis–Tanaka's conically smooth stratified spaces and Lurie's treatment in Higher Algebra, Appendix A. Grothendieck's 'déploiement' of a stratified space via such tubes anticipates AFT's 'unzip' (resolution of a stratified space to a manifold with corners). This page is only the definitional start of that programme, so the connection is implicit here.
missed.quote: muni d'une partie fermée Ṫ (le "bord" du tube) et d'une opération du monoïde topologique I=[0,1] (pour la multiplication) sur T
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck (1981-82) worked out an axiomatic, action-based mapping-cylinder-neighbourhood framework for stratified spaces. Historians tracing the origins of 'unzipping' / conical-structure ideas, and of tame topology as envisaged in the Esquisse, may want to credit this manuscript.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, careful definition of mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods via a [0,1]-monoid action. It is mathematically routine and close to known notions (Quinn, Siebenmann, Mather, AFT). Its interest is historical, as the start of Grothendieck's unpublished 'déploiement' programme from Esquisse §5, rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: Marginal label above 'de Y' is more likely ("absolu") rather than ("tubulaire"); the next page speaks of 'vois. top. conique absolu'. The phrase '(ou "cône sur Y")' is also inserted.
In the title, 'tubulaires' is crossed out and replaced by 'côniques' ('étude par voisinages côniques').
In the line 'Un voisinage ... de Y', the crossed-out words are 'tubulaire' and possibly 'conique'/'topologique'; 'est un espace topologique' does not appear struck in full in the image.
The footnote (*) reads roughly: 'Cela signifie que l'application [(I×Ṫ) ⊔ Y → T] est surjective et que T est muni de la topologie quotient de celle sur I×Ṫ [et Y]'.
Margin NB: 'La condition b) devient superflue, vu la condition 0·Ṫ⊂Y, ce qui est déjà dans c)'.
Under (5), 'λ∈[0,1[' is written with a bold bracket; the line before reads 'Notons que Ṫ est connu quand on connaît l'opération de I sur T, en posant'.
